The fields pairing is flagged by the descent into a key named 'fields' and carried to that array's elements; the paired piece is yielded where the first of title and value sits in the key order, and both keys are then spoken for. A Block Kit section's fields elements carry neither name, so they are read exactly as before.
takeOwn records the lines of the own text as it arrives, matching the whole string take already records; the entity-resolved copy is still used only for the rich_text measurement.

deviations: Blocks are read before attachments. This contradicts approved spec version 11's 'in its attachments and blocks'. The architect's ruling of 2026-10-25T06:00:29Z (Envoy message 2bcf844fa07dac607ef80e0231d96a23, confirmed in e6f1b7b7675b1d546403503bd666abc7) is its authority: Slack renders blocks as the message body and an attachment after it, so an attachment's fallback must not be the first line an agent reads.

An attachment's fields entry is emitted as one piece, 'title: value', and the single present string alone where only one of the two holds a word. This contradicts approved spec version 11's 'each entry of its fields as that entry's title and value, each non-blank one on its own line'. Same ruling as its authority: two fields sharing a value is ordinary, and the equality rule then left a label without its value, so the delivery asserted a pairing the channel does not make.

The display names are nine, not the approved seven: alt_text and author_subname join them, in the rank pretext, author_name, author_subname, title, text, alt_text, value, footer, fallback. Same ruling as its authority: an image-only Block Kit post delivered nothing at all, which is this issue's own symptom, and both strings are ones Slack renders for a person to read, which is the test approved spec version 11 states for the list.

RECORDED DEPARTURE, carried forward from round 3 and unchanged: approved spec version 11 says the walk 'never has to know the kind of a block or an attachment' and that 'the one exception is a deleted message'. The code knows the block kind rich_text by name and has two exceptions. The architect has told the human what the code does and ruled that no new spec version follows.
